newsitem.title: GERMANY: Summary of Ifo Jan German business survey.
newsitem.headline: Summary of Ifo Jan German business survey.

text.p: Following is a summary of key points in the IFO economic research institute's monthly business survey for January (sectors are west German unless otherwise stated, comparisons are against previous month):
Ifo said last week its west German climate index, the most closely watched of its business barometers, rose in January to 93.3 from December's 90.9.
Current business - picks up after two month setback
Export outlook - seen driving higher output
Orders level - demand picks up strongly

Note - Chemicals situation seen as satisfactory after orders jump; metals were upbeat, although foreign demand was less positive; pulp and paper were improving but still barely satisfactory; textiles were positive, but outlook cautious.
Orders level - stronger demand, weak output increases backlog
Export outlook - main source of hopes

Note - Machine-building situation was unchanged, orders lacking; electricals had good export prospects; vehicles were positive, more production planned; precision mechanical/optical sector were more optimistic, especially on exports; steel/light metal construction showed very good prospects.
Orders level - higher, but still lacking
Note - Carmakers expect more demand, lower production; electronics looked optimistic; precision mechanical/optical were worse, but outlook less gloomy.
Note - Clothing sector less pessimistic; shoes were worse.
Current business - less negative, but weather-hit
Orders level - up to 2.7 months output, but still too small
Personnel plans - 51 percent of firms plan job cuts
Current business - better, but still overwhelmingly negative
Current business - much better, but on balance negative
Current business - recovering, but still unsatisfactory
